previous_statement: C*-square bootstrap. Let a_n and b_n be the lower modulus and norm of gamma_n. Exact involution preservation, the K_hom e multiplicative defect from node 1.2, the exact C*-identity in the source, and the epsilon-C* inequalities in the target give, for a universal D, b_n^2 <= (b_n+D e)/(1-epsilon) and a_n^2 >= (a_n-D e)/(1+epsilon). The preliminary bounds c_0<=a_n<=b_n<=5 select the large root of the second quadratic when e is below a universal threshold; solving the two scalar quadratic inequalities yields b_n<=1+K_boot e and a_n>=1-K_boot e, with K_boot universal and independent of n. This is the asserted two-sided complete norm estimate.
new_statement: C*-square bootstrap. Let a_n and b_n be the lower modulus and norm of gamma_n. From node 1.2, ||gamma_n(X^dagger)-gamma_n(X)^dagger||<=K_hom e||X|| and ||gamma_n(X^dagger X)-gamma_n(X^dagger)gamma_n(X)||<=K_hom e||X||^2. Hence the target product-norm axiom gives ||gamma_n(X^dagger X)-gamma_n(X)^dagger gamma_n(X)||<=K_hom e[1+(1+epsilon)b_n]||X||^2. Using b_n<=5 from node 1.3.1 absorbs the bracket into a universal D. The exact C*-identity in the source and the epsilon-C* inequalities in the target then give b_n^2<=(b_n+D e)/(1-epsilon) and a_n^2>=(a_n-D e)/(1+epsilon). The preliminary bounds c_0<=a_n<=b_n<=5 select the large root of the second quadratic when e is below a universal threshold; solving the two scalar quadratic inequalities yields b_n<=1+K_boot e and a_n>=1-K_boot e, with K_boot universal and independent of n.
